questions.title: Thokozani the Farmer — Maps, Scale, Time and Distance Tables

subQuestions.questionText: A road map shows the route Thokozani will take from Mooi River to Hermannsburg in the KwaZulu-Natal Midlands. In which general direction will he travel from Mooi River to Hermannsburg?
subQuestions.memoText:
North-east

[Award 2 marks for reading the direction correctly from the map]

subQuestions.questionText: Along which two roads will Thokozani travel from Mooi River to Hermannsburg?
subQuestions.memoText:
The R622 and the R74

[Award 2 marks — 1 mark per correct road]

subQuestions.label: 1.1.3 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: What does the 'R' stand for on the road marked R33?
subQuestions.memoText:
Regional (route)

(Accept: Route.)

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.label: 1.1.3 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Through which major town does the R33 run?
subQuestions.memoText:
Greytown

[Award 2 marks for reading the town correctly from the map]

subQuestions.label: 1.1.4 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: A second map shows the straight-line distance between Mooi River and Hermannsburg. Measure the straight-line distance between Mooi River and Hermannsburg with a ruler, in cm.
subQuestions.memoText:
Approximately 15 cm (accept 14,7 cm to 15,1 cm on the printed version).

Mark 1: using a ruler to measure the straight-line distance
Mark 2: a value in the accepted range

subQuestions.label: 1.1.4 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: This map has a ratio scale of 1 : 520 000. Explain what this ratio means.
subQuestions.memoText:
1 unit of measurement on the map represents 520 000 of the same units on the ground (e.g. 1 cm on the map represents 520 000 cm in real life). The units on both sides must be the same.

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.label: 1.1.4 (c)
subQuestions.questionText: Name another type of scale that can be shown on a map.
subQuestions.memoText:
A bar scale (also accept: line scale / linear scale).

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Thokozani looks at his watch when he arrives in Hermannsburg in the morning. The watch (an analogue watch face) shows ten minutes past ten. Write the time in 24-hour format.
subQuestions.memoText:
10:10 (accept 10:09)

Mark 1: reading the analogue time
Mark 2: writing it correctly in 24-hour format

subQuestions.questionText: What type of clock face is displayed in Question 1.2.1?
subQuestions.memoText:
An analogue clock face.

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: The Hereford bull being auctioned is 3 years old. Convert the age of the bull to days.
subQuestions.memoText:
Age = 3 × 365 = 1 095 days
(Accept 3 × 365,25 = 1 095,75 days, or allowing for a leap year 1 096 days.)

Mark 1: multiplying by 365
Mark 2: answer 1 095 days

subQuestions.label: 1.2.4 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: Thokozani will transport his bull in a trailer that has enough area for the bull to feel comfortable. Explain the meaning of area in the given context.
subQuestions.memoText:
Area is the amount of flat, two-dimensional (2D) space inside the trailer floor — the surface the bull stands on.

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.label: 1.2.4 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Which is the correct formula for the area of a triangle?
subQuestions.memoText:
C — Area = ½ × base × height

[Award 2 marks for identifying option C]

subQuestions.label: 1.2.4 (c)
subQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is the correct unit of measurement for an area or surface area?
subQuestions.memoText:
B — m²

[Award 2 marks for identifying option B. Area is measured in square units.]

subQuestions.questionText: Thokozani will drive from Hermannsburg to Pietermaritzburg using a distance table. In what unit of measurement are the distances in the table measured?
subQuestions.memoText:
Kilometres (km)

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Use the distance table to determine the distance from Pietermaritzburg to Harrismith.
subQuestions.memoText:
252 km

[Award 2 marks for reading the value correctly from the distance table]

questions.title: Derrick's Braai — Perimeter, Cost, Volume, Area and Directions

subQuestions.questionText: Derrick builds a braai frame from square steel tubing. The design uses part A (1 500 mm) four times, part B (600 mm) twice, and part C (870 mm) once. Determine the total length, in mm, of tubing needed to build this frame.
subQuestions.memoText:
Total length = (1 500 mm × 4) + (600 mm × 2) + 870 mm
= 6 000 mm + 1 200 mm + 870 mm
= 8 070 mm

Mark 1: 1 500 × 4
Mark 2: 600 × 2
Mark 3: adding all the pieces
Mark 4: answer 8 070 mm

subQuestions.label: 2.1.2 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: Tubing is sold at Steel & Pipes for Africa in two lengths: 1,2 m at R70 and 1,5 m at R83,50. Part A is 1 500 mm, part B is 600 mm and part C is 870 mm. Calculate the minimum number of each length of tubing that Derrick will need to purchase to make the braai.
subQuestions.memoText:
A = 1 500 mm = 1,5 m, B = 600 mm = 0,6 m, C = 870 mm = 0,87 m.
Four A-pieces: each is exactly 1,5 m → four 1,5 m lengths.
Two B-pieces: 0,6 m + 0,6 m = 1,2 m → one 1,2 m length covers both B-pieces.
One C-piece: 0,87 m → cut from another 1,2 m length.
So: four 1,5 m lengths and two 1,2 m lengths.

Mark 1: converting the parts to metres
Mark 2: four 1,5 m lengths for part A
Mark 3: combining the two B-pieces into one 1,2 m length
Mark 4: two 1,2 m lengths in total (B-pieces + C-piece)

subQuestions.label: 2.1.2 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Use your answer from Question 2.1.2 (a) to complete the invoice by filling in the values (i) to (v). The invoice has a row for 1,2 m tubing at R70 each and a row for 1,5 m tubing at R83,50 each. (i) = quantity of 1,2 m tubing; (ii) = line total for the 1,2 m tubing; (iii) = quantity of 1,5 m tubing; (iv) = line total for the 1,5 m tubing; (v) = invoice total.
subQuestions.memoText:
(i) 2 (1,2 m lengths)
(ii) 2 × R70 = R140
(iii) 4 (1,5 m lengths)
(iv) 4 × R83,50 = R334
(v) R140 + R334 = R474

Mark 1: (i) = 2
Mark 2: (ii) = R140
Mark 3: (iii) = 4
Mark 4: (iv) = R334
Mark 5: (v) = R474

subQuestions.questionText: Derrick needs an old oil drum. The drum has a diameter of 58,4 cm and a height of 87,6 cm. Calculate, to 2 decimal places, the volume of the oil drum in cm³. Use: Volume of cylinder = π × radius² × height, with π = 3,142.
subQuestions.memoText:
Radius = 58,4 ÷ 2 = 29,2 cm
Volume = 3,142 × 29,2² × 87,6
= 3,142 × 852,64 × 87,6
= 234 679,95 cm³

Mark 1: radius = 29,2 cm
Mark 2: substituting into the formula
Mark 3: answer 234 679,95 cm³

subQuestions.questionText: This drum is said to hold exactly 200 litres of oil. Use your answer from Question 2.2.1 to determine if this is correct. (1 cm³ = 1 mℓ.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Volume = 234 679,95 cm³ = 234 679,95 mℓ
= 234 679,95 ÷ 1 000
= 234,68 litres
234,68 ℓ is more than 200 ℓ, so the statement is NOT correct.

Mark 1: converting cm³ to mℓ
Mark 2: dividing by 1 000 to get litres (234,68 ℓ)
Mark 3: correct conclusion (not correct)

subQuestions.questionText: Derrick finds a braai grid measuring 600 mm by 900 mm. Convert 600 mm and 900 mm to metres.
Calculate the area of the grid in m². Use: Area of rectangle = length × breadth.
subQuestions.memoText:
Area = 0,9 m × 0,6 m = 0,54 m²
(OR 900 mm × 600 mm = 540 000 mm² = 0,54 m²)

Mark 1: substituting into the formula
Mark 2: answer 0,54 m²

subQuestions.questionText: Derrick and his brother live in Summerstrand. In which South African city would you find this neighbourhood?
subQuestions.memoText:
Gqeberha (also accept Port Elizabeth).

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.label: 2.4.2 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: Derrick's sister is flying in from Cape Town. Using the map, name the airport where she will land.
subQuestions.memoText:
Chief Dawid Stuurman International Airport.

[Award 2 marks for reading the airport name from the map]

subQuestions.label: 2.4.2 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: She is staying at a hotel at King's Beach. Using the map, name the hotel where she is staying.
subQuestions.memoText:
Garden Court (King's Beach).

[Award 2 marks for reading the hotel name from the map]

subQuestions.label: 2.4.3 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the building indicated by the first map symbol (a bold letter 'H').
subQuestions.memoText:
A hospital.

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.label: 2.4.3 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the building indicated by the second map symbol.
subQuestions.memoText:
A school.

(Accept a named school shown on the map, e.g. Dr Cameron McIntosh / Pearson High School.)

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Give directions for the route (highlighted in yellow) from Derrick's house (A) to his brother's house (B). Give all the road names and use compass directions where appropriate.
subQuestions.memoText:
Travel south-east along Brighton Drive until you reach Admiralty Way. Turn right onto Admiralty Way and travel west until Strandfontein Road. Turn right onto Strandfontein Road, then turn right into Winchester Way, then turn right into Erasmus Drive. The brother's house (B) will be on the left.

Mark 1: south-east along Brighton Drive
Mark 2: turn right onto Admiralty Way
Mark 3: turn right onto Strandfontein Road
Mark 4: turn right into Winchester Way
Mark 5: turn right into Erasmus Drive — house on the left

questions.title: The Steyn Family Pizza Night — Recipes, Speed, Grid Maps and Boxes

subQuestions.questionText: Mr Steyn's pizza dough recipe takes 15 minutes to mix and knead, then the dough must rise for 1 hour, be split into balls and rise for another 1 hour. Determine what time Mr Steyn will have the 3 pizza bases ready if he starts at 3:42 pm.
subQuestions.memoText:
Total time = 15 min + 1 hour + 1 hour = 2 hours 15 minutes
Finish time = 3:42 pm + 2 h 15 min = 5:57 pm (17:57)

Mark 1: total time = 2 h 15 min
Mark 2: answer 5:57 pm / 17:57

subQuestions.questionText: The recipe needs 3¼ cups of all-purpose flour. Convert the amount of flour needed for the recipe to grams if ¾ of a cup of flour = 90 grams.
subQuestions.memoText:
¾ cup = 90 g, so 1 cup = 90 ÷ 3 × 4 = 120 g
Flour = 3¼ × 120 g = 390 g

Mark 1: dividing 90 g by 3
Mark 2: multiplying to find 1 cup (120 g) / multiplying by 3¼
Mark 3: answer 390 g

subQuestions.questionText: The recipe uses 1⅓ cups of warm water. Convert the amount of water used to litres if 1 cup = 250 mℓ.
subQuestions.memoText:
Water = 1⅓ × 250 mℓ = 333,33 mℓ
= 333,33 ÷ 1 000
= 0,33 litres

Mark 1: 1⅓ × 250 mℓ = 333,33 mℓ
Mark 2: converting to 0,33 litres

subQuestions.questionText: The recipe uses ¾ teaspoon of dry active yeast. Determine what percentage of a packet of dry yeast is used for this recipe, if 1 teaspoon = 2,8 grams and a packet is 10 grams.
subQuestions.memoText:
Yeast used = ¾ × 2,8 g = 2,1 g
Percentage of packet = 2,1 ÷ 10 × 100 = 21%

Mark 1: ¾ × 2,8 g
Mark 2: 2,1 g
Mark 3: dividing by 10 (the packet size)
Mark 4: × 100 → 21%

subQuestions.questionText: Mr Steyn orders pizzas from Sicily Pizzeria in Preller Square Shopping Centre. A Google map shows the delivery route from Preller Square to 11 Sergeant Street. The route is 7,5 km long and the driver takes 12 minutes. Determine the driver's average speed in km/h. Use: Distance = Speed × Time.
subQuestions.memoText:
Time = 12 minutes = 12 ÷ 60 = 0,2 hours
Speed = Distance ÷ Time = 7,5 ÷ 0,2 = 37,5 km/h

Mark 1: converting 12 minutes to 0,2 hours
Mark 2: dividing distance by time
Mark 3: answer 37,5 km/h

subQuestions.label: 3.2.2 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: The map has a grid with columns A to F and rows 1 to 4. Give the grid reference for the Steyn's house at 11 Sergeant Street.
subQuestions.memoText:
B4 (accept 4B)

[Award 2 marks for reading the grid reference correctly from the map]

subQuestions.label: 3.2.2 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: What sporting facility would you find in grid D2?
subQuestions.memoText:
Tempe Golf Club.

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.label: 3.2.2 (c)
subQuestions.questionText: Give one reason why grid references are given on maps.
subQuestions.memoText:
Grid references help users to quickly and accurately locate or identify a specific place or feature on the map.

[Award 2 marks for a valid reason]

subQuestions.label: 3.3.1 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: The pizzas come in a square-based box with sides of 30,5 cm. Determine the height (H) of the pizza box in cm, rounded to 2 decimal places, if the volume of the box is 3 544,25 cm³. Use: Volume = length × width × height.
subQuestions.memoText:
3 544,25 = 30,5 × 30,5 × H
H = 3 544,25 ÷ (30,5 × 30,5)
H = 3 544,25 ÷ 930,25
H = 3,81 cm

Mark 1: making height the subject / dividing the volume
Mark 2: 30,5 × 30,5 = 930,25
Mark 3: answer 3,81 cm

subQuestions.label: 3.3.1 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Convert the volume of 3 544,25 cm³ to m³.

subQuestions.label: 3.3.2 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: The owner adds stickers that cover the top, bottom and two sides of the box. Calculate the total surface area of the pizza box in cm² that will get stickers, if the box has base sides of 30,5 cm and a height of 3,81 cm. Use: Surface area = 2(length × width) + 2(length × height) + 2(width × height), but only the top, bottom and two sides are covered.

subQuestions.label: 3.3.2 (b) (i)
subQuestions.questionText: A diagram shows the pizza box unfolded/flattened out. What do you call this diagram?
subQuestions.memoText:
A net (a net of a rectangular prism).

(Accept: cutting die / cutting stencil.)

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.label: 3.3.2 (b) (ii)
subQuestions.questionText: Explain why the surface area of this folded-out box will be greater than the surface area of the rectangular prism box.
subQuestions.memoText:
The folded-out net includes extra material (flaps/tabs) that are needed to fold and glue/join the box together. This extra material adds area that is not counted in the surface area of the closed rectangular prism.

[Award 2 marks]

questions.title: Andrew's Holiday — Crystal Lagoon, Conversions, Floor Plans and Probability

subQuestions.questionText: The Crystal Lagoon holds 66 million gallons of water. Determine how much water, in litres, the lagoon holds if 1 gallon = 3,78541 litres. Round your answer to the nearest million.
subQuestions.memoText:
Litres = 66 000 000 × 3,78541
= 249 837 060 litres
≈ 250 000 000 litres

Mark 1: multiplying by 3,78541
Mark 2: 249 837 060 litres
Mark 3: rounding to the nearest million (250 000 000 litres)

subQuestions.label: 4.1.2 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: The tour guide says the lagoon is 1 km long, the length of 20 Olympic-sized swimming pools. An Olympic swimming pool is 50 metres long. Show, with calculations, whether the guide is correct.
subQuestions.memoText:
Length = 20 × 50 m = 1 000 m = 1 km
Therefore the guide is correct.

Mark 1: 20 × 50 m
Mark 2: = 1 000 m
Mark 3: 1 000 m = 1 km, so the guide is correct

subQuestions.label: 4.1.2 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: The tour guide also says the lagoon covers 153 football fields. The lagoon covers 27,9 acres. Show, using calculations, whether the guide is correct. (1 football field = 7 350 m²; 1 m² = 0,000247105 acres.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Convert the lagoon area to m²: 27,9 ÷ 0,000247105 = 112 907,47 m²
Number of fields = 112 907,47 ÷ 7 350 = 15,36 fields
15,36 is far less than 153, so the guide is incorrect.

Mark 1: converting acres to m² (÷ 0,000247105)
Mark 2: 112 907,47 m²
Mark 3: ÷ 7 350 m² per field
Mark 4: 15,36 fields — the guide is incorrect

subQuestions.questionText: A floor plan of a restaurant at the resort is shown, with a key for outdoor seating. How many windows are shown on the southern wall of this floor plan?
subQuestions.memoText:
1 window

[Award 2 marks for reading the floor plan correctly]

subQuestions.questionText: The floor plan shows 10 four-seater tables and 6 three-seater tables in the outdoor seating area. Determine how many people can be seated outside. Show all your working.
subQuestions.memoText:
Number of people = (10 × 4) + (6 × 3)
= 40 + 18
= 58 people

Mark 1: 10 × 4 = 40
Mark 2: 6 × 3 = 18
Mark 3: total 58 people

subQuestions.questionText: Are there separate male and female bathrooms shown on this floor plan? Give a reason for your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
No — only one restroom is shown on the plan, so there are no separate male and female bathrooms.
(Accept: Yes, if the candidate identifies two gender-specific cubicles on the plan, with a valid reason.)

Mark 1: answer (No)
Mark 2: reason based on the plan

subQuestions.questionText: Andrew leaves his table (table 2) and walks to order a cooldrink from the bar. Use only compass directions to describe his path to the bar.
subQuestions.memoText:
He walks east, then turns and walks north until the main doors, then walks north-west until he reaches the bar.
(Accept: east, then north, then west and then north to the bar.)

Mark 1: walks east
Mark 2: walks north
Mark 3: walks north-west (to the bar)

subQuestions.questionText: A lunch special offers: Main (chicken or beef), Dessert (ice cream or cake), Drink (wine or cooldrink). A tree diagram is given with some probabilities filled in: the 'cake' branch is 35% and the 'wine' branch is ¾. Complete the tree diagram by filling in the blocks (i), (ii) and (iii): (i) the missing main option, (ii) the probability of ice cream as a percentage, (iii) the probability of cooldrink as a fraction.
subQuestions.memoText:
(i) Beef (the other main option)
(ii) Ice cream = 100% − 35% = 65%
(iii) Cooldrink = 1 − ¾ = ¼

Mark 1: (i) Beef
Mark 2: (ii) 65%
Mark 3: (iii) ¼

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the probability that Andrew will have chicken, cake and wine for lunch. P(chicken) = 0,5, P(cake) = 35%, and P(wine) = ¾ regardless of previous choices. Write your answer as a percentage.
subQuestions.memoText:
P(chicken and cake and wine) = 0,5 × 35% × ¾
= 0,5 × 0,35 × 0,75
= 0,13125
= 13,125%

Mark 1: multiplying the three values
Mark 2: using the correct three probabilities
Mark 3: answer 13,125%

questions.title: Phillip the Golfer — Strip Maps, Scale and Packing Golf Balls

subQuestions.questionText: Phillip travels by car from Somerset West to George. A strip map shows the distances along the route. Determine the distance between Somerset West and George if Phillip travels along the N2 route. (Somerset West to Port Elizabeth along the N2 is 458 km; Somerset West to Cape Town is 45 km in the opposite direction.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Distance = 458 km − 45 km = 413 km
(OR reading the cumulative distances on the strip map: 734 km − 321 km = 413 km.)

Mark 1: subtracting the two strip-map distances
Mark 2: answer 413 km

subQuestions.questionText: Will Phillip drive through the town of Still Bay on his way to George if he travels along the N2 route? Give a reason for your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
No. Still Bay is not on the N2 route — it lies off the N2 (reached via the R305), so Phillip will not drive through it.

Mark 1: answer (No)
Mark 2: reason (Still Bay is not along the N2 / is on the R305)

subQuestions.label: 5.1.3 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: Phillip needs to drive to Beaufort West. Using the strip map, calculate the distance from George to Beaufort West. (George to a junction town is 67 km, and that town to Beaufort West is 187 km.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Distance = 67 km + 187 km = 254 km

Mark 1: adding the two strip-map distances
Mark 2: answer 254 km

subQuestions.label: 5.1.3 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: On which national road will Phillip travel on his way to Beaufort West?
subQuestions.memoText:
The N12

[Award 2 marks for reading the national road number from the strip map]

subQuestions.questionText: Is this strip map drawn to scale? Measure the map distances for Somerset West to Cape Town (which represents 45 km) and for Port Elizabeth to Humansdorp (which represents 78 km), and use these to support your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
On the strip map, 2 cm represents 45 km (Somerset West to Cape Town), but the same 2 cm represents 78 km (Port Elizabeth to Humansdorp).
Equal distances on the map represent different real distances, therefore the strip map is NOT drawn to scale.

Mark 1: measuring Somerset West to Cape Town (2 cm ≈ 45 km)
Mark 2: measuring Port Elizabeth to Humansdorp (2 cm ≈ 78 km)
Mark 3: conclusion — not drawn to scale

subQuestions.questionText: Phillip wins a box of golf balls. Each golf ball has a diameter of 42,6 mm. The box has internal dimensions 175 mm (length) × 130 mm (width) × 44 mm (height). Show that the box can hold 12 golf balls. Show all your working.
subQuestions.memoText:
Along the length: 175 ÷ 42,6 = 4,1 → 4 balls
Along the width: 130 ÷ 42,6 = 3,05 → 3 balls
Along the height: 44 ÷ 42,6 = 1,03 → 1 ball
Number of balls = 4 × 3 × 1 = 12 balls ✓

Mark 1: 175 ÷ 42,6 → 4 balls (rounded down)
Mark 2: 130 ÷ 42,6 → 3 balls (rounded down)
Mark 3: 44 ÷ 42,6 → 1 ball (rounded down)
Mark 4: 4 × 3 × 1 = 12 balls

subQuestions.label: 5.2.2 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine how much 'empty space' is in the box when it is filled with 12 golf balls. Write your answer in mm³. Use: Volume of sphere = 4/3 × π × radius³ (π = 3,142); Volume of a rectangular prism = length × breadth × height. Ball diameter = 42,6 mm; box = 175 mm × 130 mm × 44 mm.
subQuestions.memoText:
Radius = 42,6 ÷ 2 = 21,3 mm
Volume of one ball = 4/3 × 3,142 × 21,3³
= 4/3 × 3,142 × 9 663,597
= 40 484,03 mm³
Volume of 12 balls = 40 484,03 × 12 = 485 808,36 mm³
Volume of box = 44 × 175 × 130 = 1 001 000 mm³
Empty space = 1 001 000 − 485 808,36 = 515 191,64 mm³

Mark 1: radius = 21,3 mm
Mark 2: substituting into the sphere formula
Mark 3: volume of one ball = 40 484,03 mm³
Mark 4: × 12 → 485 808,36 mm³
Mark 5: volume of box = 44 × 175 × 130
Mark 6: 1 001 000 mm³
Mark 7: subtraction → 515 191,64 mm³

subQuestions.label: 5.2.2 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Explain why there is 'empty space' when the box is filled with the 12 golf balls. You may use a diagram to help you.
subQuestions.memoText:
The golf balls are spheres, so they cannot fill the rectangular box completely. There are gaps between the round balls where they touch each other and where they meet the flat sides and corners of the box — spheres do not pack together without leaving space.

Mark 1: idea that round balls leave gaps in a rectangular box
Mark 2: reference to the space between the balls / at the corners
